title: Attempt on An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation structural argument Result: If a geodesic deviates transversely by n^xi and the norm has quadratic curvature, the deterministic excess norm over a displacement of length n has order n*(n^(xi-1))^2=n^(2xi-1). This yields the proposed balance only after assuming random fluctuations are of the same order. Check: The power follows from norm homogeneity and the square of the relative transverse displacement. A curvature exponent kappa would instead give kappa*xi-(kappa-1). Obstruction: Both the required exponent existence and error control when replacing random passage times by the norm remain unproved for a concrete iid law here. The balance calculation is conditional, not a proof.

title: Attempt on Recurrence of sublinear vertex-reinforced walk on Z
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Recurrence of sublinear vertex-reinforced walk on Z structural argument Result: For constant w the walk is simple symmetric random walk. Starting at1 and stopping at0 or m, the harmonic function h(k)=k/m gives probability1/m of hitting m before0. Letting m tend to infinity shows that the probability of avoiding0 forever is0; by the strong Markov property returns recur indefinitely. Check: This is the standard gambler-ruin proof of the constant-weight case, not a new result. Constant weights satisfy the stated sublinear condition for any alpha in(0,1). Obstruction: For nonconstant reinforcement, position alone is not Markov and the gambler-ruin harmonic function no longer solves the conditional transition equation.

title: Attempt on Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents structural argument Result: A variance upper bound of order n/log n does not establish an exponent below1/2. Indeed log(n/log n)/(2log n) tends to1/2. Sums of floor(n/log n) independent mean-zero variance-one variables realize that variance order in an elementary model. Check: The logarithm calculation is exact in the limit; the example has additive variances. It is not asserted to be FPP. Obstruction: Known sublinear-variance estimates leave a polynomial-exponent gap. An additional power saving, and a matching lower bound for identification, are required.

title: Benaim-Rossignol (2008) gave the second proof of sublinear variance in first-passage percolation, for weight laws in the NEARLY-GAMMA class - those satisfying a log-Sobolev inequality similar to the one for the Gamma distribution - replacing Talagrand's hypercube influence inequality by an entropy argument through the Falik-Samorodnitsky inequality. The nearly-Gamma class is the class that Chatterjee's scaling relation later assumes.
body:
i.i.d. edge weights on Z^d whose law lies in the nearly-Gamma class: it satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality similar to that for the Gamma distribution
d >= 2

WHY THIS NODE MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN THEOREM: 'nearly Gamma' is not a throwaway regularity word. It is the named distributional class introduced here, and it is exactly the hypothesis that Chatterjee (2013) carries into the scaling relation chi = 2 xi - 1 and that Auffinger-Damron (2014) then removed for one of the two inequalities. Anyone quoting either of those two results without naming this class has dropped a hypothesis.
SOURCE: Benaim, M. and Rossignol, R. (2008), 'Exponential concentration for first passage percolation through modified Poincare inequalities', Ann. Inst. H. Poincare Probab. Statist. 44, 544-573. Read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), tex line 1170 (attribution and class description) and tex line 2959 (the Chatterjee link).
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim, and a WEAK one - flagged deliberately. The survey line read describes the class and the method; it does NOT state the theorem. So two things are missing here: the precise form of the log-Sobolev condition, and the exact form of the conclusion. Note also that the paper's own title is about exponential CONCENTRATION, not variance; the survey characterises it as the second proof of sublinear variance, which is consistent (concentration on the n/log n scale gives the variance bound) but is the survey's framing, not a quoted theorem. Anyone consuming this node for anything load-bearing must read the paper.

title: Chatterjee (2013) proved the KPZ scaling relation chi = 2 xi - 1 for first-passage percolation on Z^d - but ONLY for his own strengthened definitions of the exponents, ONLY under the assumption that those strengthened exponents exist, and ONLY for 'nearly Gamma' weight laws. The Auffinger-Damron-Hanson survey records that Chatterjee's exponents are not known to exist for ANY distribution of passage times, so as of the survey the relation is established for no distribution at all, and proving it remains open.
body:
the exponents are Chatterjee's STRONGER definitions, not the standard chi, chi', chi_x, xi or xi_x
those strengthened exponents are ASSUMED to exist - and are not known to exist for any weight law
the weight law is 'nearly Gamma' (the Benaim-Rossignol log-Sobolev class)
i.i.d. non-negative edge weights on Z^d under moment assumptions
the curvature status is NOT settled by this node: the survey says only that a strong definition of the exponents was introduced partly because the relation should need uniform positive curvature of the limit shape, which is unproven. Whether Chatterjee's own theorem carries a curvature hypothesis was NOT verified by lane P4 - see the flag in the body

THIS NODE EXISTS BECAUSE THE RESULT IS ROUTINELY MISQUOTED. The four misquotations, named:
  (1) 'Chatterjee proved chi = 1/3.' No. The relation is between two unknown exponents. Getting       chi = 1/3 out of it needs xi = 2/3, which is exactly as open as chi = 1/3.
  (2) 'chi = 2 xi - 1 holds for FPP.' Not for the standard exponents. It holds for Chatterjee's       strengthened ones, and only if they exist.
  (3) 'The relation is known for some distribution.' The survey is explicit: 'as of today, there       is not a single distribution of passage times where we know that [chi = 2 xi - 1] holds',       and it poses finding one as an open question.
  (4) 'It is universal, hence distribution-free.' The universality is a statement ABOUT the       relation (independent of d and of the law within the class), not a licence to drop the       nearly-Gamma hypothesis. Auffinger-Damron removed nearly-Gamma for the inequality       chi <= 2 xi - 1 only.
THE AUTHOR'S OWN SUMMARY: 'This article gives a rigorous proof of this conjecture assuming that the exponents exist in a certain sense' (abstract, arXiv:1105.4566v3).
METHOD: break a geodesic into segments and compare the passage time to a sum of nearly i.i.d. variables through an approximation scheme, then trade off approximation error against the variance; the nearly-Gamma hypothesis is what lets that optimisation be carried out.
CURVATURE - THE ONE PLACE THIS NODE IS MOST LIKELY TO BE SUBTLY WRONG, FLAGGED ON PURPOSE. The survey says two things: that the relation 'should be valid only under the unproven assumption of uniform positive curvature of the limit shape', and that this 'is one of the main reasons for the introduction of a strong definition of exponents'. It is tempting to read that as 'Chatterjee's theorem therefore has no curvature hypothesis', and an earlier draft of this node did. That is an INFERENCE from the survey's motivation sentence, not a quoted hypothesis list, and lane P4 did not verify it. THE CHECK THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: read the hypothesis list of the main theorem of arXiv:1105.4566v3 and record whether a curvature or limit-shape condition appears in it. Until then, treat the curvature status of this theorem as unknown here.
Related, and this part IS quoted: the survey adds that with a different curvature exponent kappa one would expect chi = kappa xi - (kappa - 1), reducing to chi = 2 xi - 1 at kappa = 2.
SOURCE: Chatterjee, S. (2013), 'The universal relation between scaling exponents in first-passage percolation', Ann. of Math. (2) 177, no. 2, 663-697; arXiv:1105.4566v3. Hypothesis set read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), section 'The scaling relation chi = 2 xi - 1', tex lines 2943-2963 (in particular 'Chatterjee's exponents are not known to exist for any distribution of passage times' and "Assuming that the distribution is 'nearly Gamma'...").
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim for the complete hypothesis set, with the existence assumption independently confirmed against Chatterjee's own abstract. Lane P4 did not read the Annals paper.

title: Corollary 2.15 of arXiv:2603.24423: First passage percolation preserves sublinearly Morse boundaries
body: [Corollary 2.15 of arXiv:2603.24423, 'First passage percolation preserves sublinearly Morse boundaries'] Let $X$ be an infinite connected graph with bounded degree, and let $o$ be some vertex of $X$. Assume $\nu(\{0\})=0$. Let $\gamma:[0,n]\rightarrow X$ be any finite self avoiding path of length $n$, such that $d(\gamma,o)\leq D\cdot n$. Then the image of $\gamma$ in $X_{\omega}$, is a quasi-isometric image of $\gamma$ whose constants depends only on $\omega$, i.e. there exists constants $q(\omega),Q(\omega)$ such that, $\frac{1}{q}\cdot\ell(\gamma)-Q(\omega)\leq\ell_{\omega}(\gamma)\leq q\cdot\ell(\gamma)+Q(\omega)$

title: Damron-Houdre-Ozdemir (2022): a POLYNOMIAL fluctuation lower bound does exist in planar first-passage percolation, but for a different observable - T_n, the minimal passage time between two opposite sides of an n by n square - under a curvature assumption and for exponentially distributed weights, where the fluctuations of T_n are at least of order n^{1/8-epsilon} for every epsilon > 0. This is NOT a bound on the point-to-point passage time T(0,x), where the best lower bound is still logarithmic.
body:
the observable is T_n, the minimal passage time between two opposite sides of an n by n square - a minimum over crossings, not a point-to-point passage time
a curvature assumption on the limit shape (unproven in first-passage percolation)
the edge weights t_e are exponentially distributed
d = 2

WHY A SEPARATE ARGUMENT WAS NEEDED, in the authors' words: 'previous arguments to bound the fluctuations of T(x,y) only give a constant lower bound for those of T_n (even assuming curvature)', so they represent T_n as a minimum of cylinder passage times and use the Markov property to get finer distributional information. The minimum-over-crossings structure is the whole difficulty and the whole difference.
COROLLARY they state: the first polynomial lower bounds on higher central moments of the discrete torus passage time, under the same curvature assumption.
THE MISQUOTE THIS NODE EXISTS TO BLOCK: 'polynomial variance lower bounds are known in FPP'. They are known for this observable, under an unproven curvature assumption, for one weight law (extended by Dembin-Elboim to absolutely continuous laws). Nothing polynomial is known unconditionally for Var T(0,x).
SOURCE: arXiv:2204.06592v1, 'Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation on the square, tube, and torus'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source. The abstract states the observable, the curvature hypothesis, the weight law and the exponent; the proof was not read.

body: [Definition 2.17 of arXiv:2603.24423, 'First passage percolation preserves sublinearly Morse boundaries'] The topology on ∂sX is defined as follows: let β be a κ Morse sublinearly quasi-geodesic ray for some κ. An equivalence class a ∈∂sX belongs to U(β, r) if, for any (q, Q)-quasi-geodesic ray α ∈a, where mβ(q, Q) is small compared to r with respect to κ, we have the inclusion α|r ⊂Nκ(β, mβ(q, Q)).

title: Definition 2.7 of arXiv:2603.24423: First passage percolation preserves sublinearly Morse boundaries
body: [Definition 2.7 of arXiv:2603.24423, 'First passage percolation preserves sublinearly Morse boundaries'] Let (X, dX) be a proper geodesic metric space and Z ⊆X a closed subset, and let κ be a concave sublinear function. A map πZ : X →P(Z) is a κ-projection if there exist constants D1, D2, depending only on Z and κ, such that for any points x ∈X and z ∈Z, diamX({z} ∪πZ(x)) ≤D1 · dX(x, z) + D2 · κ(x). A κ-projection differs from a nearest point projection by a uniform multiplicative error and a sublinear additive error.

title: Dembin-Elboim (2025): for planar first-passage percolation with i.i.d. weights uniform on {a,b}, 0 < a < b < infinity, the event that the minimal left-right crossing time tau(n,k) of the square [0,n]^2 with vertical fluctuations bounded by k exceeds its median is NOISE SENSITIVE whenever k <= n^{1/2-epsilon} - unconditionally, improving Ahlberg-De la Riva's n^{1/22-epsilon} - and, under a curvature assumption, for all k <= n; the same methods give Var T_n >= n^{1/4-epsilon} for the minimal left-right crossing, extended from exponential to absolutely continuous weights.
body:
planar first-passage percolation on Z^2, i.i.d. weights uniform on {a,b} with 0 < a < b < infinity
the k <= n^{1/2-epsilon} noise-sensitivity result is UNCONDITIONAL
extension to all k <= n^{1-epsilon} needs the limit shape not to be a polygon with a small number of sides - and follows unconditionally when a and b are sufficiently close
extension to all k <= n needs a stronger curvature assumption
the variance bound Var T_n >= n^{1/4-epsilon} needs the curvature assumption; it is for the minimal left-right crossing T_n = tau(n,n), not the point-to-point passage time

CONSISTENCY CHECK WITH DAMRON-HOUDRE-OZDEMIR: a variance lower bound n^{1/4-epsilon} is a standard-deviation lower bound n^{1/8-epsilon/2}, which matches their fluctuation exponent n^{1/8-epsilon}. The two results agree; Dembin-Elboim's contribution on that half is the weight class, from exponential to absolutely continuous.
WHY THIS MATTERS TO A CHAOS PROGRAM: this is the strongest unconditional noise-sensitivity statement available on the LATTICE, and noise sensitivity is the same family of object as the geodesic disorder chaos that Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly telescope in the continuum. The technique is different from earlier work: a small-ball probability estimate in the tail, obtained by perturbing the weights for tail events with a Mermin-Wagner type estimate.
SOURCE: arXiv:2505.03211v1, 'Noise sensitivity and variance lower bound for minimal left-right crossing of a square in first-passage percolation'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source. The abstract separates the unconditional range from the two conditional extensions and states the weight class for each; the proof was not read.

title: FPP chi=1/3 campaign - CORRECTED 2026-08-22 by lane P3's referee pass; supersedes the 2026-08-15 fire-4 novelty-downgrade row and restates it whole. ONLY ONE PHRASE CHANGED: that row read "(C3) is constant-A doubling hence wall-equivalent". Wall-equivalence is not an exact biconditional - constant-A doubling delivers beta = O(1) through CRUX 9.8's true-ratio route at the blocks the geodesic meets with probability of order one, not at the near-band small-p blocks, and the converse gives the M-fold ratio rather than the 2-fold one. The row's own conclusion is unaffected: (C3) at M = 2 IS verbatim constant-A doubling, so the continuity route's marginal content is TRANSPORT only. THE REST STANDS AS WRITTEN. Quantile interpolation F_t^{-1} := (1-t) F_0^{-1} + t F_1^{-1} between non-degenerate laws on [a,b] stays on [a,b], preserves non-degeneracy and has modulus eta(h) <= h(b-a), so doubling for ONE such law would give Var = O(n^{1-log2/logM}) for EVERY such law. THE NOVELTY CLAIM STAYS DOWNGRADED to new in this specific form, not new in kind, on the declared literature pass: (i) Chatterjee, "The universal relation between scaling exponents in first-passage percolation", Annals of Math 177 (2013), arXiv 1105.4566, proves chi = 2 xi - 1 and states it is universal, independent of dimension and of the weight law under moment assumptions, so distribution-independence of FPP exponents is an established theme; (ii) Damron-Hanson-Sosoe, arXiv 1306.1197 (PTRF), get sublinear variance for general distributions directly under only 2 + log moments, a condition strictly weaker than the bounded support the continuity lemma needs, with no transfer argument at all. The transfer principle is therefore narrower than the state of the art on the axis it trades in. It is not vacuous - the target transferred is the polynomial n^{1-eps} nobody has for any single law - but it must never be presented as a new idea about universality. chi = 1/3 UNMOVED.
